pairs: Non zeles mulierem sinus tui,
You should not be jealous of the wife of your bosom,
ne ostendat super te malitiam doctrinæ nequam.
lest she reveal, because of you, the malice of a wicked lesson.
Non des mulieri potestatem animæ tuæ,
You should not give authority over your soul to a woman,
ne ingrediatur in virtutem tuam,
lest she obtain your strength,
et confundaris.
and then you would be confounded.
Ne respicias mulierem multivolam,
You should not look with favor on a woman with many desires,
ne forte incidas in laqueos illius.
lest perhaps you may fall into her traps.
Cum saltatrice ne assiduus sis,
You should not be continually in need of entertainment,
nec audias illam,
nor should you be persuaded by it,
ne forte pereas in efficacia illius.
lest perhaps you may perish by its effectiveness.
Virginem ne conspicias,
You should not stare at a virgin,
ne forte scandalizeris in decore illius.
lest perhaps you may be scandalized by her beauty.
Ne des fornicariis animam tuam in ullo,
You should not give your soul, in any way, to fornicators,
ne perdas te et hæreditatem tuam.
lest you destroy yourself and your inheritance.
Noli circumspicere in vicis civitatis,
Do not choose to look around in the streets of the city,
nec oberraveris in plateis illius.
nor should you wander along its thoroughfares.
Averte faciem tuam a muliere compta,
Avert your face from an ornate woman,
et ne circumspicias speciem alienam.
for you should not gaze upon strange beauty.
Propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt:
Many have perished because of the beauty of a woman;
et ex hoc concupiscentia quasi ignis exardescit.
and by this, desire is kindled like a fire.
Omnis mulier quæ est fornicaria,
Every woman who is a fornicator will be trampled down,
quasi stercus in via conculcabitur.
like the filth in the street.
Speciem mulieris alienæ multi admirati,
Many, by admiring the beauty of the wife of another,
reprobi facti sunt:
have become reprobate.
colloquium enim illius quasi ignis exardescit.
For familiarity with her flares up like a fire.
Cum aliena muliere ne sedeas omnino,
You should not sit down at all with another man’s wife,
nec accumbas cum ea super cubitum:
nor recline with her on a couch.
et non alterceris cum illa in vino,
And you should not argue with her over wine,
ne forte declinet cor tuum in illam,
lest perhaps your heart may turn toward her,
et sanguine tuo labaris in perditionem.
and by your emotion, you would be toppled into perdition.
Ne derelinquas amicum antiquum:
You should not abandon an old friend.
novus enim non erit similis illi.
For a new one will not be similar to him.
Vinum novum amicus novus:
A new friend is like new wine.
veterascet,
It will grow old,
et cum suavitate bibes illud.
and then you will enjoy drinking it.
Non zeles gloriam et opes peccatoris:
You should not envy the glory and wealth of a sinner.
non enim scis quæ futura sit illius subversio.
For you do not know what may be his undoing in the future.
Non placeat tibi injuria injustorum,
The injury of the unjust should not please you,
sciens quoniam usque ad inferos non placebit impius.
knowing that, until they are in hell, the impious will not please.
Longe abesto ab homine potestatem habente occidendi,
Keep yourself far from a man having the power to kill,
et non suspicaberis timorem mortis.
and then you will not have the fear of death suspended over you.
Et si accesseris ad illum,
But if you do approach him,
noli aliquid committere,
do nothing to offend,
ne forte auferat vitam tuam.
lest perhaps he may take away your life.
Communionem mortis scito,
Know that this is a communion with death.
quoniam in medio laqueorum ingredieris,
For you would be entering the midst of snares,
et super dolentium arma ambulabis.
and walking upon the arms of the grieving.
Secundum virtutem tuam cave te a proximo tuo,
According to your ability,
et cum sapientibus
be cautious of your neighbor,
et prudentibus tracta.
and treat him as the wise and prudent would.
Viri justi sint tibi convivæ,
Let just men be your companions,
et in timore Dei sit tibi gloriatio:
and let your glory be in the fear of God.
et in sensu sit tibi cogitatus Dei,
And let the thought of God be in your mind,
et omnis enarratio tua in præceptis Altissimi.
and let all your discourse be on the precepts of the Most High.
In manu artificum opera laudabuntur,
Works will be praised for the hands of the artists,
et princeps populi in sapientia sermonis sui,
and a leader of the people will be praised for the wisdom of his words, yet truly,
in sensu vero seniorum verbum.
the word of the elders will be praised for its understanding.
Terribilis est in civitate sua homo linguosus:
A man full of words is a dread to his city,
et temerarius in verbo suo odibilis erit.
but one who speaks rashly will be hated for his word.
